r-0001.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
r-0001.notes: Covers residential dwelling units in Berkeley with no building-level limits (year built, unit count, building type, owner type or tenancy length). The exemptions concern types of algorithm products (aggregated anonymous data publishers, affordable housing rent/income limit tools, market research for financing, appraisals or software development) and not building characteristics, so they cannot be tested against address data and no tests are generated.

r-0002.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
r-0002.notes: Coverage depends on the owner or agent charging a screening fee for a credit report and application processing, not on any building-level attribute. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated, so the rule applies to all residential rentals in Berkeley.

r-0003.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
r-0003.notes: Coverage is all residential rental property in Berkeley with no exemptions and no building-level limits. The 'existing tenants' condition is a tenancy status that the engine cannot see, but it does not limit the building type, size, or age, so no test is created for it.

tests.value: fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
tests.source_text: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
tests.note: Coverage depends on Rent Ordinance status (exempt units are outside the ordinance); the engine cannot determine this from assessor data.

tests.source_text: A unit where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord is exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy.
tests.note: Shared kitchen/bath exemption applies only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy; the engine cannot see owner residence or shared facilities.

r-0004.notes: Coverage is tied to the Rent Ordinance (fully or partially covered units, including government-owned or subsidized units required to register). No year, unit-count or building-type limits are stated in the text, so none are invented. Operative date is not stated.

tests.note: Tenancies that began on or after 2025-01-01 with Costa-Hawkins rents are excluded. The engine cannot see tenancy start date or how the rent was set, so this returns unknown. The test is a placeholder (tenancy_months >= 0) so it can be explained as unknown.

tests.source_text: Eligible landlords of units under Berkeley rent stabilization
tests.note: Coverage depends on whether the unit is subject to the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance (e.g., rental units not exempt under BMC 13.76). The engine cannot determine this from assessor data.

r-0005.notes: The AGA applies only to units under Berkeley rent stabilization, and not to tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins. The building-level facts the engine knows (year_built, units, building_type) are not stated as limits in the text, so no tests are written for them.

tests.source_text: owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
tests.note: Exemption applies only to owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units; the engine cannot see owner residence. Not exempt if the building has more than 3 units.

tests.source_text: limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties
tests.note: Limited exemption; subsidy status is not visible to the engine.

tests.source_text: units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
tests.note: Tenancy situation not visible to the engine.

tests.source_text: units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
tests.note: Lease terms not visible to the engine.

r-0006.notes: Coverage is all rental housing providers in Berkeley with no building-type limits. Exemptions for owner-occupied 1-3 unit buildings, public housing/Section 8, owner move-back leases, and sublet/roommate situations are included as tests. The lifetime sex offender exemption concerns the applicant rather than the building, so it is not expressed as a test.

tests.note: Golden Duplex status cannot be determined from the assessor data.

tests.note: Owner and tenancy facts are not visible to the engine.

tests.note: ADU and owner-occupancy facts are not visible to the engine.

tests.note: The assessor use code may not identify university-owned housing.

tests.source_text: nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Cooperative status is not visible to the engine.

Fully or partially covered status cannot be turned into a single test, so only the exemptions are encoded. Exemption tests resolve to unknown because the engine cannot see owner, tenancy, or ADU facts.

r-0008.title: [notice-only] Boston Housing Stability Notification Act

tests.source_text: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
tests.note: Institutional exemption that the engine cannot see from assessor data; building_type does not identify these facilities.

r-0008.notes: Coverage is all units in Boston where a landlord or foreclosing owner intends to end a tenancy, so there are no building-level limits on year, units, or building type. The only limit is the institutional exemption, which the engine cannot evaluate. Notice-only rule with no just-cause protection.

tests.note: Coverage depends on funding/subsidy status, which the engine cannot see; result will be unknown.

tests.source_text: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt the policy.
tests.note: Applicant-specific and law-specific exemptions (including preemption by conflicting federal/state criminal-history requirements) cannot be evaluated from address data.

r-0011.notes: Applies only to housing providers with DND funding/land or BPDA IDP income-restricted units, and via the Affirmative Marketing Program, not all Boston landlords. No building-type, year built, or unit-count limits are stated. Effective date is not stated.

r-0012.title: Boston fair housing protection for renters using rental assistance
r-0012.notes: Coverage is limited to housing in the City of Boston (jurisdiction-level) and to renters or applicants using rental assistance (a tenant characteristic, not a building-level limit). No building-level limits or exemptions are stated, so no tests are emitted.

r-0013.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
r-0013.notes: General antitrust rule, not rental-specific. It states no building-level limits (year built, units, building type), so no building tests apply. The only exemption excludes end consumers from the definition of 'person', which concerns the actor and not the property. The common-pricing-algorithm definition (two or more users, competitor data) and the conspiracy or coercion elements are conduct conditions the engine cannot check against address facts.

r-0014.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
r-0014.notes: The rule covers any landlord or agent charging an applicant (including a guarantor or cosignor) to rent a residential unit, with no building-level limits on year built, units, or building type. The exemptions are not building-level coverage limits. One concerns federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees, which are not preempted. Others are the reusable screening report option and the no-refund rule for applicants denied under established criteria. The last is that the fee is not treated as an advance fee or as security. None of these narrow which addresses are covered, so no tests were created.

r-0015.title: California Tenant Protection Act - just cause for termination

tests.source_text: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible to the engine; 24 months applies in the added-adult-tenant case.

tests.source_text: housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years
tests.note: Exempt if the certificate of occupancy was issued within the previous 15 years, so the rule applies only when it is 15 or more years old.

tests.source_text: separately alienable property (e.g. single-family home) not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice
tests.note: Exemption for separately alienable property such as single-family homes and condos whose owner is not a REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC and who gave written notice. Owner identity is unknown to the engine. It cannot apply to buildings that are not separately alienable.

tests.source_text: owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex
tests.note: Owner-occupied exemption for single-family homes (renting up to two units or bedrooms) and duplexes. Owner occupancy is unknown to the engine. It cannot apply to larger buildings.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted affordable housing
tests.note: Subsidy and deed-restriction status is unknown to the engine.

tests.source_text: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and licensed care facilities; school dormitories; shared bathroom/kitchen with owner-occupant; ... mobilehome owners
tests.note: Use-type exemptions the engine cannot express from assessor data.

tests.source_text: Does not apply to property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later local ordinance that is more protective
tests.note: Depends on local ordinances; the engine cannot evaluate this.

r-0015.notes: Rule is generally applicable to residential real property but has many exemptions. Exemptions the engine cannot see (owner type, tenancy length, deed restriction, use type, local ordinance) are encoded so unknown results can be explained. The certificate-of-occupancy exemption uses year_built as a proxy with the cutoff year unknown. The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01.

r-0016.title: Statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act), Civ. Code § 1947.12

tests.source_text: The cap does not apply to housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome)
tests.note: Certificate of occupancy date is unknown to the engine; year_built is a proxy. Mobilehome tenancies are not subject to this exemption.

tests.source_text: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing
tests.note: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing is exempt; subsidy status is not visible to the engine.

tests.source_text: separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and where the required written exemption notice was given
tests.note: Separately alienable property (single-family, condo) is exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and the written exemption notice was given. Owner identity is unknown to the engine. Multi-unit apartment buildings are not separately alienable, so the exemption cannot apply to them.

tests.source_text: a duplex in which the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence (neither unit an ADU or JADU)
tests.note: The duplex owner-occupancy exemption cannot be seen by the engine. It is impossible if the building is not a duplex.

tests.source_text: dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school; housing under a local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap
tests.note: Dormitory use and stricter local rent control cannot be determined from the engine's data.

r-0016.notes: Covers residential real property, including mobilehome park tenancies. The 15-year certificate of occupancy exemption does not apply to mobilehomes. Mobilehome tenancies are covered only for increases on or after 2021-02-18. The cap applies only to subsequent increases after the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains. Mobilehome homeowners are exempt. The section is operative from 2024-04-01 and repealed as of 2030-01-01. The query date of 2026-10-01 is within the operative period.

r-0017.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
r-0017.notes: Coverage is housing decisions by landlords in California using criminal history information, with no exemptions and no building-level limits (no year built, unit count, building type, owner type, tenancy or funding conditions). It therefore applies to all residential rentals in the state.

r-0018.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-tenant credit/income screening limits (FEHA)

tests.source_text: the credit-history and income-standard rules in subd. (o) apply only where there is a government rent subsidy
tests.note: Only the subsidy-tenant credit-history and income-standard provisions depend on a government rent subsidy; the engine cannot see subsidy status, so this is unknown. The core source-of-income ban applies to owners of any housing accommodation.

r-0018.notes: The source-of-income discrimination ban covers owners of any housing accommodation with no building-level limits. Only the credit-history alternative-evidence and income-standard rules are conditioned on a government rent subsidy. The statement that inquiring about income level or source is not discrimination, and that landlords may verify employment, request references and verify identity, describes permitted conduct, not a building exemption, so no tests were added for it.

r-0019.title: California residential security deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
r-0019.notes: The rule covers security for any residential rental used as the tenant's dwelling and states no building-level limits. The two-month small-landlord cap depends on owner_type (natural person or LLC of natural persons, at most two properties and four units) and the tenant's service-member status, which the engine cannot see. The six-month advance-payment allowance depends on lease term, which the engine also cannot see. The July 1, 2024 application date concerns when security was collected, not the building, so it is not a building test. No tests are generated; the engine would report the rule as applying to all residential rentals in CA.

r-0020.title: Cambridge policy order initiating ban on algorithmic rent-setting services
r-0020.notes: Coverage is described as residential property management companies in Cambridge (loosely 'large or corporate owners/managers'), but no building-level limits (year built, unit count, building type) are stated, so no tests are produced. The rule is only a pending policy order, not an enacted ordinance. The 'large or corporate' descriptor is not a stated threshold, so it was not turned into a test.

r-0021.title: [notice-only] Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge M.C. ch. 8.71)
r-0021.notes: Coverage is all residential rental agreements, including single units and tenants at will. The exemptions are for hospital, skilled nursing or health facility units, non-profit substance-abuse treatment facilities, and Short Term Rental Units. The engine cannot see these from assessor data, so they are not turned into building-level tests. No year, unit-count or building-type limits are stated.

tests.source_text: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.

tests.source_text: when the owner lives there
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible to the engine; the exemption is impossible if the building is not a 2-family dwelling (units > 2).

r-0022.notes: Coverage is all rental housing transactions in Cambridge, with one exemption: 2-family dwellings where the owner lives. The engine cannot see owner occupancy, so results for duplexes/2-unit buildings will be unknown. The ordinance text itself was not provided, only a secondary summary.

r-0023.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
r-0023.notes: Covers any residential dwelling unit (any primary residence) in Hoboken. The exclusion of medical/long-term care and detention facilities is not expressible with the assessor data (building_type), so no test is generated and no building-level limits are stated. Possible preemption by NJ FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) is an interaction, not a coverage test.

r-0024.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
r-0024.notes: Coverage applies to all residential landlords with no building-level limits and no exemptions. The 10% year-over-year renewal increase is a transaction-level trigger, not a building characteristic, so it is not expressed as a test.

r-0025.title: Hoboken Rent Control: cost-of-living increase cap (Code § 155-5)
r-0025.notes: The text states no building-level limits or exemptions. Coverage is limited to dwellings to which Chapter 155 applies, but that applicability and the exemptions are defined elsewhere in the chapter and not in this capture, so no tests were invented. Actual coverage may be narrower than this record shows.

r-0026.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
r-0026.notes: No coverage conditions or exemptions are stated, so the rule is treated as covering all residential rentals in Jersey City. The possible preemption by New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) is an interaction the source does not address, so it is not encoded as a test. The source is secondary and gives only 'effective June 2025' with no exact day.

r-0027.notes: Coverage is taken from a secondary news description only. The exemptions for real estate agents and for non-colluding algorithm users depend on the actor's conduct, not on building attributes, so they are not encoded as building tests. The MLS exclusion outcome is unclear. Possible preemption by the NJ FAIR Act is an interaction and not a coverage test.

The page states no year_built or unit-count limits for JCO, and says it can apply to post-October 1, 1978 buildings and to a single-family dwelling, so no such tests were added. The RSO carve-out is flagged as an untestable condition.

The Mom & Pop reduced amounts (four or fewer units, owner or family occupancy) only change the payment amount and do not limit coverage, so no unit-count test was added. The resident manager and natural disaster exemptions concern the circumstances of the eviction and cannot be expressed with address-level data.

Condo/townhome tenancy exemption is flagged via a tenancy_months test the engine cannot evaluate, defeated for non-condo building types. The luxury exemption (rent on or before 1978-05-31) and market-rate resets after voluntary move-out, at-fault evictions or buyout agreements are unit-level facts the engine cannot see. Replacement units under LAMC 151.28 and mobile homes in mobile home parks are not captured by year_built. Allowable percentage is in a linked PDF and not captured.

r-0032.title: LAMC Sec. 45.67 Prohibited Activities (source-of-income discrimination)

r-0034.title: H.5222 - An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
r-0034.notes: No coverage conditions or exemptions are stated; the source is a status page only and the bill text is not reproduced. Scope should be verified in the bill itself. The bill is not enacted as of 2026-10-01.

r-0035.title: S.2983 An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (bill)
r-0035.notes: No coverage conditions or exemptions are stated in the capture, so no building-level tests are produced. The operative bill text, definitions, exemptions and effective date are not available. S.2983 is a proposed bill and is not enacted, so the actual scope may differ once the text is reviewed.

r-0036.title: Broker fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker
r-0036.notes: Coverage is limited by the type of actor (licensed brokers or salespersons, or persons finding dwellings for a fee), not by any building-level attribute. No exemptions stated, so no building-level tests are needed.

r-0037.title: No application fees by landlords (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
r-0037.notes: The rule covers lessors of residential tenancies statewide and states no building-level limits (no year, unit-count, or building-type conditions). The broker exemption turns on who collects the fee (a licensed broker complying with 254 CMR 7), not on any property characteristic, so it cannot be expressed as a building test. The engine cannot see the party's status, so it is not encoded.

r-0040.title: Source-of-income / housing subsidy discrimination ban (M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
r-0040.notes: The text states no building-level limits and lists no exemptions. It applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, so no tests are needed. Recipient status (public assistance or housing subsidy) is a tenant-level fact, not a building-level coverage limit.

tests.note: Engine cannot see tenancy purpose or length; this is a short-term vacation/recreational rental exclusion and does not limit coverage of ordinary residential leases or tenancies-at-will.

r-0041.notes: The statute covers residential leases and tenancies-at-will statewide with no building-level limits (no year built, unit count, or building type conditions). The only exemption is for vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less, which the engine cannot evaluate from address data, so it is recorded as an 'other' test.

r-0042.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
r-0042.notes: The act covers every rental residential dwelling unit owned by anyone owning one or more units. No building-level limits are stated: no year built, unit count, building type or tenancy-length thresholds. The exclusions for inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention or correctional facilities are use-based and cannot be checked against assessor data. The software and data-tool exemptions (non-AI spreadsheets, unprocessed-data databases, research use, free public estimates, brokerage databases, government affordability controls) concern tools and conduct, not buildings. Section 9 sets the effective date at 2027-07-01, so the act is not yet in effect on the 2026-10-01 query date.

tests.source_text: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
tests.note: Exemption applies only to a two-family dwelling with the owner living in the other unit. The engine cannot see owner occupancy. A building with units > 2 can never qualify for this exemption.

tests.source_text: rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Exemption applies only to renting rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling. The engine cannot see owner occupancy. A building with units > 1 can never qualify for this exemption.

r-0047.notes: Coverage is all property, with no building-level limits. Two narrow owner-occupancy exemptions are encoded as owner_type tests that return unknown. The religious-organization preference and the older-persons housing (familial status) exemptions do not bear on source-of-income coverage for ordinary rentals, so they are not encoded as tests. No effective date is stated in the source.

r-0048.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)

The federally assisted housing meth-manufacture and lifetime sex offender registry allowances are narrow permitted considerations, not coverage exemptions, so they are not expressed as tests.

The engine cannot see owner occupancy or tenancy length, so these will return unknown for buildings with 2-3 units. No effective date stated in the document.

r-0054.title: San Diego Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant's Source of Income

tests.source_text: Does not apply where the owner or a family member resides in the same residential building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant (§98.0804).

The exemption for acts necessary to comply with program requirements concerns conduct, not building characteristics, so no test is made for it. The defeated_if of units > 4 is a conservative assumption, not stated in the text, since a shared kitchen or bathroom with the owner is implausible in larger buildings; it may be removed if the reviewer prefers to avoid inventing limits.

r-0055.title: S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C - Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices
r-0055.notes: Coverage is all residential units in San Francisco with no building-level limits and no exemptions. The definition of 'algorithmic device' describes the prohibited conduct, not a building characteristic, so it is not turned into a test. The effective date of October 14, 2024 is before the query date of 2026-10-01, so it adds no limit.
